segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Ah, a battle! Do try to do something worth a verse.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Gather round, gather round, and mind the pointy end.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Every good song has a fight in the middle. Here's ours.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Ha! That'll rhyme with something.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Hm. We'll leave that out of the ballad.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Oh, that's the second verse, right there!

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: And here the singer pauses, out of respect.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: No, no, no. That's not how this one goes!

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Oh, this is the sad part, isn't it. I hate the sad part.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Bless you. You'll get a chorus all your own.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Someone's growing into their legend.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: And they lived, and the song went on. For now.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: There's a last verse to the Song of the Seven. Nobody's sung it in two hundred years. I'll find it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Sleep now, sleep now, the river is wide, and the fire keeps watch on the other side.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Songs don't burn. That's why I keep them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Hum along if you know it. Nobody ever knows it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: You'll want to tell this one well, when you're old. I'd start practising.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Lark. Songkeeper. I keep the Warden songs, the only history the fire can't burn.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: She's writing him down so the fire can't have him. That's all a song is, really. Writing someone down where nothing can burn them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: So. Mirewood. Did the Court sing for you? Half the Warden songs ended up in those reeds. I can hear my own verses in them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Ysolde offered me a verse for a memory. I said no. She wasn't pleased. The fey aren't used to hearing it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: It wasn't the last verse anyway. The fey don't have it either. Whoever kept that one never used the fire.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Not here. Ask me again somewhere colder. Some things you only say where your breath shows.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: But watch the hooded one by the door. They've been a step ahead of you since the ford, and a step ahead of me for twenty years.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Quickly, before she's offended. Drink half the water. Pour the rest on the sand, for the farms that burned.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: That's the point. You give the sand something you can't spare. Then they give you everything they have.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Every note. Well, you mangled the second verse, but only a little.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: While you sleep under this cloth, every Scarwalker in the Sunscar will bleed for you.
